correctness.rationale: Multiplication by e_i detects its coefficient, so the annihilator is exactly Kz. Pairwise zero products and independence of the cyclic squares force the nonzero images of distinct natural basis vectors to have disjoint coordinate supports in the quotient. Spanning forces exactly m singleton supports and one nonzero vector in Kz, giving the claimed form and converse over any field. The coefficient calculation gives exactly the cycle edges and the spoke set S. With the cyclic path and, for nonempty S, one spoke s→z as a spanning tree, signed closed-walk lengths generate the subgroup with generators m and i−s (i∈S), since the height differences telescope and each non-tree arc closes along the tree. This also treats m=2, where the arcs are distinct. For empty S the only contributing component is the directed cycle. A nonempty singleton realizes m and {0,d} realizes every proper divisor d with the sink attached. Directly, in dimension three the one-spoke and two-spoke bases yield balances 2 and 1 on connected graphs. For the dimension bound, degenerate dimension two has at most one row with a nonzero square, so only a loop can give positive balance, and then it is 1. In nondegenerate dimension two one can either use the cited invariance theorem or argue directly: independent squares force monomial changes of basis; proportional nonzero squares give both natural basis squares in the same line, nonzero in each row, hence a loop in every natural basis. Dimension one is immediate. The frozen checker's finite-field source and recorded checks were inspected, not executed; the all-fields proof is decisive. The small connected witness can be replayed by the two explicit basis squarings in RESULT.md line 47.

value.rationale: This answers a stated basis-invariance question negatively with the smallest possible dimension for distinct positive balances, while ruling out loss of connectivity as the cause.
